How We Help Families Through Complex Wrongful Death Litigation The litigation process can be time-consuming and stressful, involving many different rules and procedures. The following are only a few things a GJEL wrongful death attorney in California will do during litigation: Filing the Lawsuit A wrongful death lawsuit has many requirements and must be persuasive enough to successfully present your legal case and stand up to challenges by the other party. You must also comply with strict procedural rules, including properly serving all defendants with notice of the lawsuit. If service of process is not handled correctly, your case can be dismissed even if liability is clear. Gathering Evidence Evidence in your favour is gathered in many different ways, including through investigators, depositions, document requests, and more. Challenging the Other Side’s Defenses The other party will certainly raise legal defenses to avoid liability. Our wrongful death attorney will answer back to challenge those defenses and protect your rights to a recovery. Negotiate a Favorable Settlement The majority of wrongful death lawsuits are settled out of court but this does not mean you should accept a settlement that is too low just to avoid trial. GJEL’s fatal accident attorneys will effectively use new arguments and evidence to negotiate until you receive the settlement offer you deserve. We are not afraid to litigate your case and hold wrongdoers responsible. If your case involves criminal conduct, you can pursue a civil wrongful death claim while the criminal case is still pending. You do not have to wait for a criminal outcome to seek justice and compensation. Represent You at a Jury Trial If the liable party refuses to make an adequate settlement offer, your wrongful death lawyer in CA will present your case at a trial, which involves strict rules of evidence and procedural requirements. This takes place in a courtroom with a judge and jury. You May Be Able To File a Wrongful Death Suit in California In California, when someone’s death is the result of wrongful behaviour or negligence, surviving family members can file what is known as a “wrongful death” lawsuit in civil court. You may be eligible to file even if your relationship to the deceased is not straightforward. In addition to spouses, domestic partners, children, and parents, California law can allow putative spouses, stepchildren, financially dependent family members, and in some cases the personal representative of the estate to pursue a wrongful death claim. Eligibility depends on your specific relationship and circumstances. In addition to spouses, domestic partners, children, and parents, California law also allows certain other parties to file a wrongful death claim. This can include putative spouses who believed in good faith they were married, stepchildren, dependents who relied financially on the deceased, and in some cases the personal representative of the decedent’s estate. Family relationships are not always simple, and eligibility can depend on the specific facts of your situation. Immigration status does not affect your right to file a wrongful death lawsuit. California law allows families to pursue wrongful death claims regardless of citizenship or documentation status. An experienced wrongful death lawyer can explain your rights and help you and your family seek justice for the pain you are experiencing Your immigration or citizenship status does not prevent you from filing a wrongful death lawsuit in California. You have the same right to pursue compensation regardless of documentation status.. In this article, we provide a basic overview of wrongful death laws in California. We’ll cover the elements of a wrongful death claim, who can file a wrongful death lawsuit, and the different types of damages that are available to a successful plaintiff. We also discuss how the statute of limitations can impact your claim. This post is designed to give you basic information and should not be relied upon in the absence of advice from a qualified California wrongful death attorney. If you have questions about your rights or your family’s rights, contact one of our accidental death lawyers right away. Elements of a Wrongful Death Case In legal terminology, an “element” is an essential building block of a case. For someone to succeed in a case, the evidence must establish all of the required elements. In a wrongful death lawsuit in California, the following elements must be proven. The death of a human being; That was caused by another’s negligence, or with intent to cause harm; and The surviving family members are suffering financial losses as a result of the death. GJEL accidental death attorneys will discuss and help you fortify each of these elements for your case. Element One: What Kinds of Accidents or Intentional Acts Cause Wrongful Death? Several different kinds of accidents can lead to wrongful death. These include car accidents, commercial truck accidents, bicycle accidents, pedestrian accidents, the use or consumption of dangerous or defective products, prolonged exposure to toxic chemicals, medical malpractice by a doctor or healthcare facility, fires, and other types of fatal accidents. Intentional acts such as a deadly assault, manslaughter, murder, arson, or other deliberately harmful act also may be the basis of a wrongful death claim. Element Two: Was the Death Caused by Negligent or Intentional Conduct? The causation element is critical in a wrongful death claim. To recover damages, you must be able to show that your loved one’s death was actually caused by the negligent or intentional conduct of the defendant. For example, you cannot sue a hospital just because your loved one died of cancer there. There is no wrongful death liability when someone dies purely from natural causes. However, if you can show that your loved one died of cancer as a result of prolonged exposure to cancer-causing chemicals in his or her workplace, you may be able to sue the former employer for wrongful death due to carelessness. Because causation in a wrongful death lawsuit can be difficult to establish, it is important to hire a lawyer for wrongful death who has extensive experience taking wrongful death lawsuits to trial and obtaining successful verdicts for his or her clients. Element Three: Have Survivors Suffered a Loss? You and your family must be able to establish that you have suffered losses as a result of your loved one’s death. These might include the loss of your loved one’s affection and emotional support, financial support, or contributions to the household. Other types of losses include money you spent or will need to spend to take care of your deceased loved one’s medical expenses and funeral costs. A wrongful death law firm can help you understand the full value of your wrongful death claim and will carefully calculate the amount of damages to which you are entitled. At GJEL, we can help you through this difficult time by fighting for justice and compensation on behalf of your loved one. What Damages are Available in a Wrongful Death Lawsuit? The wrongful death statute in California is relatively vague when it comes to the damages that surviving family members can recover after proving a wrongful death. If a survival action is also filed, the estate may recover damages for medical expenses incurred before death, lost wages prior to passing, and the pain and suffering your loved one experienced between injury and death. In fact, the law simply states that any “just” damages may be available in a particular situation. Many different parties may bring wrongful death claims in CA, including spouses, children, stepchildren, parents, and other potential heirs. The damages that each different party can recover will vary depending on their own specific and personal losses from the death. The law gives the court discretion to determine the rights of each party to certain damages. For the above reasons, it is impossible to say exactly what damages you may receive without a thorough evaluation of your situation. You should also be aware that punitive damages are generally not available in wrongful death cases, except in limited situations involving especially egregious or criminal conduct. These damages are intended to punish extreme wrongdoing rather than compensate your family. While the best way to learn about potential damages in a wrongful death case is to consult with an experienced wrongful death in California. Some Losses Which You May Be Able to Recover Reasonable funeral and burial expenses The estimated amount of income and benefits the deceased person would have earned in their lifetime had the accident not occurred Loss of financial support for the household Loss of services around the household, including cleaning, landscaping, cooking, caring for children, and other everyday tasks and contributions to the family Loss of intangible support, including love and affection, encouragement, moral support, guidance, attention, and more. Some parties may have contributed to funeral expenses while others may not have. In addition, older parents may have lost financial support but not any household services if they did not live in the same place as the deceased. As you can see, the situations can vary widely depending on the specific circumstances. Calculating Damages in a Wrongful Death Case Once you have determined the type of damages that may be available in your wrongful death case, it becomes necessary to calculate the exact amount you want to seek. If more than one family member is entitled to compensation, damages are typically awarded as a single lump sum. If you and other claimants cannot agree on how to divide the award, the court may determine allocation on your behalf. Some damages are much easier to calculate than others–for instance, to determine funeral and burial costs, you should simply examine all of the bills and receipts you received from the funeral home and other service providers. Note that only reasonable expenses will be reimbursed. This means that if you throw a lavish funeral and reception for your loved one, you may likely only receive a portion of the costs back. Factors to Calculate Lost Future Earnings The age of the deceased and how many more years they would be expected to work; The education, skills, and abilities of the deceased; The deceased’s potential for promotions, raises, and other adjustments to income throughout the course of their career; Inflation and how wages and earnings would be adjusted over the years; and The benefits and retirement account contributions the deceased would have received. Considering all of these factors into one calculation can be complicated and you will often need the assistance of an occupational and economic expert to reach an accurate estimate. Experts are also used to determine the monetary value of household services lost, as well as the loss of affection, love, and other intangible support. Our California wrongful death attorneys have the resources needed to obtain expert analysis to ensure you receive a fair and just result in your case and always seek the maximum possible damages available. Contact Our California Wrongful Death Attorneys Now Frequently Asked Questions About Wrongful Death Cases in California How long do wrongful death cases take in California? In our experience, most wrongful death cases in California take between one and two years to resolve. Some cases settle sooner, while others take longer if a trial is required. Our attorneys guide families through every stage so you always know what to expect and where your case stands. What damages can families recover in a wrongful death claim? Families may recover compensation for funeral and burial expenses, final medical bills, lost income and benefits, lost future earnings, and the loss of love, companionship, guidance, and support. Our attorneys work with financial and economic experts to ensure every category of loss is fully documented and pursued. Can I pursue a wrongful death case if the person responsible has died? Yes. Even if the at-fault person has passed away, our attorneys can pursue a claim against their estate and any applicable insurance policies. We regularly handle these cases so families can still recover the compensation they deserve. Do I need to hire a wrongful death attorney right away? Yes. Waiting can seriously damage a wrongful death case. Evidence can be lost, witnesses may become harder to locate, and California law imposes strict deadlines. Our attorneys step in immediately to protect your family’s rights and preserve critical proof. Where do you file a wrongful death claim in California? Wrongful death lawsuits are filed in civil court, usually in the county where the fatal incident occurred or where the defendant resides. Our attorneys file cases throughout California and understand how each local court operates. Whose insurance or estate pays damages in a wrongful death lawsuit? In most cases, the at-fault party’s insurance policy provides the primary source of recovery. If insurance coverage is limited or unavailable, our attorneys pursue claims against the person’s estate and any other legally responsible parties to maximize compensation. What are the insurance policy limits in a wrongful death case? Policy limits control the maximum amount an insurance company will pay on a claim. One of the first steps our attorneys take is identifying every available insurance policy. If limits are low, we aggressively investigate additional sources of liability such as employers, manufacturers, or third parties. How much is a wrongful death case worth in California? There is no fixed value for a wrongful death case. The value depends on factors such as the person’s age, income, life expectancy, medical expenses, funeral costs, and the impact of the loss on surviving family members. Our attorneys have secured recoveries ranging from hundreds of thousands to tens of millions of dollars depending on the facts. Who pays for funeral expenses and final medical bills in a wrongful death case? Funeral and burial expenses and final medical bills are pursued as part of the wrongful death claim. These costs are typically paid from a settlement, insurance policy, or court judgment, rather than remaining the family’s sole responsibility. Our attorneys ensure these expenses are fully included. What if more than one family member wants to file a wrongful death claim? California law allows only one wrongful death lawsuit per person’s death, but multiple eligible family members may join together in that single case. Our attorneys guide families through this process to ensure everyone’s rights and interests are properly represented. How long does it take for families to receive wrongful death settlement funds? After a wrongful death case settles and all required paperwork is completed, settlement funds are generally issued within several weeks. Any outstanding medical liens or costs are handled first, and the remaining funds are then distributed to the family. What is your fee if you take my wrongful death case? We handle wrongful death cases on a contingency-fee basis. This means you pay nothing upfront and owe us nothing unless we win compensation for your family. All fee terms are clearly explained before representation begins.
